_doc: REKS Studio merged multi-sector catalog ABI for Psi4 (reksMM.bin); hashed into REKS_LAYOUT_HASH, loader fails closed on mismatch. v3 carries all spin sectors of one (N,M) in one blob: global deduplicated microstate table, sector-blocked configs, a SectorEntry table. Header spin2/n_sa_default/off_sa_default are removed; they live per sector in SectorEntry. v5 replaces the fixed PairDeps record by column arrays plus one varint window block per pair, and drops b50_pairs (it is the has_scaling column). v7 widens every ABSOLUTE blob offset a record carries to 64 bits -- SectorEntry.off_sa_default and the DiagDeps windows: their ceiling is the blob's own size, so uint32 bounds the whole format at 4 GiB. REKS(10,10) writes 62.73 GiB and died on off_sa_default after 50.4 h of compute. v8 makes every id into a pool that grows with the config pairs LOCAL to the sector that emitted it, and gives SectorEntry the ten origins to read them back: a sector never reuses an earlier sector's row, so its slice of each pool is contiguous and its ids are exactly [0, its own row count). Pool indices stay int32 -- the pair-major channels store them at that width -- and the whole-run ERI rows that overran it on the (10,10) projection (1.03x headroom) clear it 2.4-fold per sector. The origins are also what lets a reader map one sector's slice of a pool and leave the rest on disk. v9 stops the file repeating what it can name. A value row carried an 8-byte coefficient, and a REKS(10,10) catalog holds 1 893 distinct coefficients against 39.7 million such rows: the run's palette now travels once as coeff_pool and the row carries its id, with the FON window's length above it in the same int32 (see value_meta) -- 312 MB of a 1.17 GB file, and the alignment hole of the old LagrTerm with it. A term window and a cell window TILE the pool they point into, so their (start, length) pairs become one CSR boundary array each. A weight row's key is its own row number and its key_j the -1 of a diagonal block row; a 1-RDM row's key_i is a CSR pointer over the configs. The microstate label is the occupation pattern spelled a second time and the delta label is printed nowhere, so both columns and the 1.8 MB of strings behind them are gone. Nothing here changes a number the catalog computes: every field removed is derived, repeated or unread. v10 re-cuts a value row into one packed int64. The row carried a 20-bit coefficient id and an 11-bit FON window length in one int32, with the window's start beside it in a second -- and REKS(12,12) mixed-scheme reaches some 5e9 factor rows against the 2.1e9 that start could address, so emission died at 38 % of the blob. The widths were also mis-shared: the length cannot exceed kFonMaxFactors = 34, a compile-time bound, yet held 2047. The word now spends 18 bits on the id, 6 on the length and 39 on the start -- 5.5e11, two hundred times what (12,12) needs -- in the same eight bytes, so no catalog grows by a byte. The packed fock/eri row key is re-split at the same time: its halves were 31 bits each, while an index part is a distinct orbital row (hundreds) and a value part one row per surviving term (2.7e9 at REKS(12,12) mixed-scheme), so the 63 bits now go 31 to the index part and 32 to the value part -- 32 being the whole of what the interner's value slot allows either of them. The key is internal to the sweep and no blob field changes with it.
_pair_windows_doc: Each pair owns one contiguous block in pair_win_data starting at pair_win_off[p]; the windows follow in `order` with the element counts the pair's PairShape gives, so the block is read by decoding it and no per-window offset is stored. e_pack holds two ints per element.
_pack_columns_doc: fock_pack and eri_pack are selector rows (idxpart id, valpart id) indexed by the row id fock_idx/eri_idx carry. Each is stored as two delta+zigzag varint columns, the whole idxpart column then the whole valpart column, n_*_pack_rows values each, spanning *_pack_bytes from off_*_pack.
_value_meta_doc: The five coupling value pools and the diagonal term pool name their coefficient by its id in coeff_pool instead of carrying the double. A row is one int64 word: bits [0, coeff_bits) the id, the next fon_n_bits the length of the row's FON window, the next fon_off_bits its start, the sign bit clear. Every ceiling already bounds the generator's own key -- the id at coeff_bits is the width the emission's value-pool key packs it in, a window holds at most 2*(2*8+1) = 34 factors, and the start addresses 5.5e11 factor rows -- so the record narrows nothing.
